events.title: INC-2231
events.content: INC-2231 (3 Dec, payouts delayed 47 minutes). Symptom: payout-service started throwing 'FATAL: remaining connection slots are reserved for non-replication superuser connections' and PgBouncer cl_waiting climbed past 20 at 14:22. Root cause: a deploy at 14:05 added a code path that opened a pgx transaction and then called the partner bank HTTP API inside it; when the bank's p99 went to 9 seconds the transactions sat idle-in-transaction and ate all 40 slots of the PgBouncer pool on payouts-db. I rolled back at 14:41 and re-drove 12 pending payout batches by hand at 14:52. Fixes: moved the HTTP call outside the transaction, set idle_in_transaction_session_timeout = 30s on the payouts role, and wrote a small go vet analyzer that flags http.Client calls between Begin and Commit. Impact: 312 payouts delayed, no money lost, no SLA credits. Marcus thinks the fix is enough and does not want to raise the pool size; I wanted 60, left as an open question.
The payments API has an SLO of 99.95% availability and p99 latency under 400 ms, measured monthly. Last quarter we hit 99.97%.

events.title: INC-2287
events.content: INC-2287 (5 Feb, Sev2). Symptom: idempotency lookups on the payments API went from 8 ms to 2.8 s p99 at 15:12 and merchants retried, producing 14 duplicate charges. Root cause: the ElastiCache node (cache.r6g.large, 13 GB) hit maxmemory because we cached the whole response body (average 18 KB) under each idempotency key, and a campaign from the merchant Lumio Retail pushed 600 req/s. With allkeys-lru, keys for in-flight requests were evicted, so a retry looked like a new request. Detection came from a merchant support ticket before our own alert fired, which is the embarrassing part. Fix: store only a SHA-256 of the request plus the status code (under 200 bytes), TTL 24h, and move the whole idempotency store back to Postgres with a unique index on (merchant_id, idempotency_key). The 14 duplicates were refunded manually the same evening, total AUD 3,870. Follow-ups: add a memory alert at 70% on the Redis node, and write ADR-024 reversing ADR-017.

Priya classed INC-2287 as a Sev2 and the customer-facing postmortem went to three merchants: Lumio Retail, Tallow & Co and Bayside Grocers. She wants me to author ADR-024 and present it at the architecture forum on 12 February.

events.title: INC-2340
events.content: INC-2340 (1 April, 02:40): ledger-writer pods were OOMKilled repeatedly, 17 restarts in 40 minutes, and ledger lag peaked at 11 minutes. Root cause: after the Go 1.24 upgrade a retry loop in the batch flusher never cancelled its context when Postgres was briefly slow, so goroutines piled up (pprof showed 3,400 of them) each holding a 500-line batch and its prepared statements, until the 1Gi limit was hit. Kafka retained everything so there was no data loss. Fix: defer cancel() in the flusher, set GOMEMLIMIT=800MiB, raise the pod memory limit to 1.5Gi, and expose pprof on a port that is only reachable through kubectl port-forward. I also added a goroutine-count panel to the Grafana ledger dashboard with an alert above 1,000. Sam reviewed the limits and agreed the 1.5Gi request was fine for the node pool.

events.title: INC-2412
events.content: INC-2412 (5 Aug, 16:40): a rebalancing storm on the ledger.events consumer group in the reporting service pushed consumer lag to 2.4 million messages. Root cause: max.poll.interval.ms was 5 minutes but the reporting consumer's batch handler took up to 7 minutes during month-end exports, so the broker kicked it out of the group, it rejoined, and every other consumer paused for the rebalance. It looped for 50 minutes. With only 12 partitions we also could not scale out past 12 consumers to catch up. Fix: moved the heavy export out of the poll loop into a worker queue, raised max.poll.interval.ms to 15 minutes, switched to cooperative-sticky assignment, and grew the topic from 12 to 24 partitions on the MSK cluster (3 x kafka.m5.large). Nothing was lost but the finance team's daily report was 3 hours late. Marcus pointed out we should have a lag alert per consumer group, which I added.

events.title: Registry rollout
events.content: Schema registry rollout plan for Hannah. Phase 1 (October): deploy Apicurio 2.6 in the kp-prod-apse2 cluster with a Postgres storage backend on a small RDS instance, and register the existing ledger.events Protobuf messages with BACKWARD_TRANSITIVE compatibility. Phase 2 (November): add Buf breaking-change checks to the CI pipeline for the ledger-events repo, and make ledger-writer register schemas at startup behind a feature flag. Phase 3 (December): migrate the reporting service and the risk engine to read through the registry, with a dual-read period of two weeks where both the old shared Go package and the registry decode run side by side and mismatches are logged. Risks: Apicurio is another thing to run and patch; Glue would avoid that but locks us to AWS client libraries. Success metrics: zero consumer breakages from schema changes in Q1 2027 and onboarding a new consumer in under a day. Cost is about USD 120 a month for the extra instance and storage.
